name: Guardian CS-7 SecureSpray
description:
The Guardian CS-7 SecureSpray is a mid-tier dual-agent aerosol combining a 2% CS (2-chlorobenzalmalononitrile) lachrymatory compound with a 0.5% OC amplifier, suspended in a hydrofluorocarbon propellant rated for stable discharge across a temperature range of -10°C to 45°C. It is the standard-issue crowd and personal control spray for contracted security firms, private building management companies, and licensed corporate security auxiliaries operating in Tier 2 and Tier 3 zones. The canister is significantly larger than consumer-grade options — approximately 180ml — with an ergonomic overmold grip, a rotating nozzle head offering cone or stream patterns, and a tamper-evident seal ring for accountability tracking.

The CS component produces a rapid and pronounced tearing and burning response in mucosal tissue, with secondary effects including coughing, chest tightness, and disorientation. The OC amplifier extends the inflammatory response and increases effectiveness against partially augmented targets whose respiratory systems remain biological. Guardian markets the CS-7 as a 'compliance facilitation tool' in its B2B literature, and most purchasers are institutional — building security firms, transit authority contractors, and mid-tier corporate campus guards. Individual licensing is available but carries a background verification requirement.

The CS-7 has a reasonably strong reputation for reliability and consistent performance, though critics within the civil liberties advocacy space have raised concerns about its deployment in enclosed residential environments, where the CS agent can persist for several hours and affect uninvolved residents through shared ventilation systems.
legality: Licensed — individual purchase requires personal security license; institutional purchase available under commercial security contractor registration
specifications:
Primary agent: 2% CS (2-chlorobenzalmalononitrile)
Secondary agent: 0.5% oleoresin capsicum
Propellant: HFC-134a blend
Net volume: 180ml
Nozzle modes: cone (3m spread) / stream (5m direct)
Effective range: 1–5m depending on mode
Spray duration: approx. 12 seconds continuous
Operating temperature: -10°C to +45°C
Price: Φ85
tactical_use: Used by security personnel to control individuals who are non-compliant or physically aggressive without resorting to impact weapons or conducted energy devices. The stream setting allows targeted application against a single subject at moderate range; the cone setting is used for crowd dispersal or when precise aim is not possible. Standard security doctrine calls for a one-second burst followed by a verbal compliance command, with additional bursts applied as needed. Deployment in confined spaces requires post-incident ventilation protocols.
cultural_context: The CS-7 is known colloquially as 'blue guard' due to its blue canister livery and association with corporate security auxiliaries — the 'blue guards' who patrol Tier 2 and 3 commercial zones. Among working-class residents, being sprayed with a CS-7 is called 'getting the warden' and carries a humiliating social connotation — it implies you were compliant enough to be sprayed but not dangerous enough to be shot. Security workers view it as a mundane professional tool, like a radio or a badge scanner.
story_hooks: A CS-7 canister recovered from a crime scene has a serial number that traces back to a security contractor who officially disbanded two years ago — but the canister's manufacture date is last month.

physical_description.visual_profile: A utilitarian cylindrical aerosol canister with a distinctly professional security aesthetic—bulkier than consumer pepper spray, with a prominent grip section that dominates the lower two-thirds. The rotating nozzle head sits proud of the canister body, suggesting industrial-grade functionality. Overall impression is serious, institutional, and designed for repeated deployment.
physical_description.dimensions: Height: 18.5cm | Diameter: 5.2cm | Grip width: 3.8cm | Nozzle head projection: 1.8cm
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty but well-balanced when gripped—approximately 320g when full. The overmold grip distributes weight toward the palm, making it feel substantial without being unwieldy. Noticeable heft suggests a full 180ml payload.
physical_description.primary_material: Aluminum alloy canister body; rubberized polymer overmold grip; injection-molded polycarbonate nozzle turret
physical_description.finish: Matte black powder coat on canister with subtle industrial texture; brushed aluminum band beneath grip section for accountability serial plate mounting; high-gloss black overmold grip with subtle surface ribbing
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: matte black canister body | Accent: brushed aluminum maintenance band, bright safety-yellow rotating nozzle indicator dot, red tamper-evident seal ring at base
physical_description.grip_texture: Rubberized polymer with aggressive crosshatch texture for secure handling even with wet or augmented gloves; slightly tacky to touch, designed for rapid deployment and retention
distinctive_features: Rotating dual-pattern nozzle head with tactile detents for cone/stream selection—visible click-stops at 90-degree intervals
Bright safety-yellow circular indicator dot on nozzle showing active pattern (position indicates current mode)
Tamper-evident seal ring at canister base—red, breakable band with serial number visible when broken
Accountability band with serial plate: brushed aluminum collar just beneath grip with laser-etched Guardian logo and alphanumeric code
Pressure gauge dot on canister shoulder—translucent window showing remaining contents (green/amber/red)
Discharge nozzle bore slightly recessed, protected by raised rim to prevent accidental activation
Subtle GUARDIAN logo embossed on upper canister body in raised chrome lettering
Wear-resistant finish shows micro-scratches and minor abrasions from holster carry and field use typical of institutional deployment
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: GUARDIAN logo in raised lettering on upper third of canister; serial plate on brushed aluminum accountability band below grip (laser-etched); regulatory compliance stamps (including GLMZ municipal codes) on lower canister; safety warnings in white printed text on back face
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained institutional condition—lightly scuffed, showing evidence of regular holster carry and occasional field deployment but not battle-worn. Nozzle turret occasionally shows minor polymer discoloration from residual agent exposure. Grip remains tacky and functional. Seal ring intact on active units, broken on recently-deployed canisters.
